name: Belotero Balance

lead: Belotero Balance is a soft hyaluronic acid filler from Merz used for fine lines, folds and the hollow under the eyes. People choose it for a smoother, brighter-looking area soon after injection.

Its cohesive polydensified matrix spreads evenly in the skin and adds subtle volume, then degrades over time. A split-face randomized comparison of three HA formulations for nasolabial folds followed patients for 12 months, and trials cover darker skin types and under-eye hollows. It is studied for lines and hollows rather than structural projection, and forum posters also discuss filler as a precursor or stand-in for surgery.

paras: A licensed clinician injects fine lines or the under-eye area in an office visit with little downtime. People repeat treatments as the gel absorbs, and it can be dissolved with hyaluronidase.
Filler complications across the category include bruising, nodules and rare vascular events. It is a prescription medical device, and results are temporary.

chain: Soft cohesive HA integrates in skin
angle.text: Belotero Balance is a soft hyaluronic acid filler used for fine lines and under-eye hollows, giving a smoother, brighter-looking area soon after injection. The cohesive gel blends into the skin to fill shadow and lines. A 12-month randomized comparison exists for nasolabial folds.

lead: Belotero Balance is a hyaluronic acid (HA) dermal filler from Merz that uses cohesive polydensified matrix (CPM) technology, designed to integrate smoothly into the skin. It is used for fine lines and superficial areas such as nasolabial folds, and has been studied for the under-eye (infraorbital) hollow. [1][2]
Published studies include a split-face randomized comparison of three HA formulations for nasolabial folds with 12-month follow-up and trials in darker skin types and infraorbital hollows. [3][4][5]
infobox: Fine lines, nasolabial folds, infraorbital hollows

paras: A literature review describes the CPM gel family and its use for soft-tissue augmentation and rejuvenation. [1] Laboratory studies rank fillers by cohesivity and rheology and place Belotero Balance among FDA-approved HA fillers evaluated. [6][7][8]
In-vitro studies have examined how Belotero and other commercial HA fillers are degraded by hyaluronidase. [9][10]

Analyses of FDA adverse-event reports and litigation, and a cross-sectional study of complications and lawsuits involving injectable facial fillers, describe vascular and other complications for fillers as a category. [11][12]

A prospective split-face randomized study compared three HA formulations for nasolabial folds over 12 months. [3] A literature review summarizes CPM filler studies. [1] A technique article describes lip enhancement approaches. [2]

Registered trials include a post-approval nasolabial fold study (n=117), a study in Fitzpatrick skin types IV-VI (n=93), an infraorbital hollow pilot (n=66), a lidocaine pain study (n=52) and comparisons in perioral lines with Restylane Silk. [4][5][13][14]
